title: Market Replay Studio
subtitle: Queue dynamics, inventory control and adverse selection you can inspect.

cases.label: Balanced flow
cases.title: Watch the queue. Account for every fill.
cases.description: Balanced flow: a price/time-priority book, cancellable orders, inventory-constrained quoting and stale quotes. Replay the managed policy, then compare net results across sixteen paired seeds.

charts.title: Marked equity before final liquidation · seed 1729
Liquidated outcome over independent paired seeds

method: Orders match at the resting price, best price then FIFO. Partial fills and owner-checked cancellations use the same book as the replay, with integer price/quantity accounting.

All trader accounts conserve aggregate cash and inventory after every batch. Agent fees are a separate external charge of 0.05 tick/unit; the net ledger includes that fee sink. Final liquidation executes through five refreshed LP levels, ten units each, starting at mid ±3 ticks. Price slippage and fees are included.
Inventory is bounded at ±20 units through quote sizing. This legacy delayed policy refreshes every five batches; timestamped message latency is studied in the separate cancel-latency cases.

Sixteen independent seeds compare policies with identical pre-generated price, order-size and flow draws. In the adverse regime, 70% of eligible flow is informed by the next reference move; this privileged signal is unavailable to the agent.
limitations: Synthetic event flow and exogenous reference prices are not calibrated exchange data. No claim of profitable live trading is made.
Background refreshes may trade against stale agent quotes; losses from those crossings are included. The agent does not control market impact or reference prices.
Latency is measured in event batches, not network nanoseconds. Hidden liquidity, auctions, credit limits and exchange-specific order types are omitted.
Recorded replay uses seed 1729; summary uncertainty uses separate paired seeds 100–115. Mark-to-mid equity differs from final liquidated net.

cases.label: TWAP / balanced
cases.title: Does spreading execution reduce arrival-price cost?
cases.description: Execute 120 buy units over twelve batches. Compare equal-time cumulative targets with an immediate sweep that retries residuals. Both face identical external events and finite displayed depth. Lower shortfall is better; completion and residual risk matter too.

metrics.label: TWAP arrival-price shortfall
metrics.note: Includes fees and terminal-marked unfilled opportunity cost

method: data: Synthetic; independent pre-generated external paths shared by policies
fee_per_executed_unit: 0.05
arrival: Reference midpoint before first external event
liquidity: Five levels per side, 10 units each, mid +/-3..7; fully refreshed every batch
event_order: Refresh background, external IOC, parent IOC; no resting parent remainder
shortfall: s*(notional-filled*arrival) + fees + s*residual*(terminal_mid-arrival); s=+1 buy, -1 sell
residual: Unexecuted positive parent units; marked at terminal reference, not liquidated
baseline: Release entire parent at batch zero and retry residual every batch
twap: Cumulative floor(Q*(t+1)/T) target each batch; carry deficits, no forced terminal fill
uncertainty: 16 independent paired seeds 200..215; Student t(15) 95% CI for TWAP minus baseline; negative favors TWAP
boundaries: No calibrated flow, permanent impact, latency, funding, borrow cost, hidden depth, or fee tiers
limitations: Synthetic reference prices and full background replenishment are exogenous; depth depletion is real within a batch but there is no persistent impact. Findings depend on this strong replenishment assumption.
Residual units are not trades. Their signed terminal midpoint opportunity cost is a valuation convention and does not guarantee executable completion. Negative costs are retained.
TWAP is a deterministic equal-time cumulative schedule with catch-up, not a calibrated optimal policy. The baseline can consume more depth earlier and retries until the same deadline.
Recorded replay uses seed 1729; table means and paired t intervals use independent seeds 200–215. No real-market edge is established.

cases.label: Cancel latency / balanced
cases.title: What trades while a cancellation is in flight?
cases.description: Compare immediate cancellation with six-unit cancellation delay, holding two-unit submission delay fixed. Replay the delayed policy; inspect stale executed units and liquidated net costs.
method: Integer timestamps; messages execute by arrival time then enqueue sequence. Submissions receive exchange IDs on arrival. Cancellation removes only its target; surviving FIFO priority is retained.

Each ten-unit batch: background refresh at 0; agent cancel and quote request at 1; new quotes arrive at 3; external aggressive flow at 5; delayed cancels arrive at 7. No privileged cancellation precedence on ties.

A stale fill executes at/after its cancellation request. Stale midpoint markout is signed quantity times (current reference midpoint minus trade price); it may be positive and is not additional P&L or causal loss.
Reserve inventory capacity for every live order until cancellation arrives; absolute inventory limit 20. Fees 0.05 tick/unit; final position liquidates through refreshed finite depth at mid +/- 3..7.

Sixteen fresh paired seeds 300..315 share external draws; Student-t 95% interval on delayed minus immediate liquidated net. Replay seed 1729 is separate; raw results include the first two batches of message receipts.
limitations: Synthetic fixed delays and full background replenishment, without exchange clock calibration, jitter, market impact, hidden liquidity or funding costs.
Delayed cancels overlap old and new quotes; risk reservation changes replacement sizes. This is the total effect of the specified policy, not an isolated estimate of adverse-selection loss.
Cancellation that arrives before submission misses and is not remembered by the exchange; retries must be explicit. Stale classification describes intent even if an earlier cancellation missed.
The legacy delayed-refresh cases measure refresh cadence and remain separate from these timestamped message-delay cases.

cases.label: Fresh seeds / balanced
cases.title: Does inventory control's cost persist on fresh paths?
cases.description: Confirm the existing symmetric, inventory-skew and five-batch refresh policies on seeds 400–431. Compare liquidated net and average absolute inventory; negative differences mean lower net or lower exposure respectively. No policy is retuned on these paths.

charts.title: Liquidated net / ticks
charts.xlabel: Independent paired seed (lines are visual guides)

charts.title: Mean absolute inventory / units
charts.xlabel: Independent paired seed (lines are visual guides)

method: Frozen specification: docs/confirmation-plan.json; engine SHA-256 is checked before every run. Three original policies, 240 batches, fixed sample of 32 seeds 400..431, excluding previous study and replay seeds.
Within a regime and seed, all policies use identical pre-generated reference, side, size and informed-flow draws. The seed is the independent statistical unit; regimes reuse seeds and are not pooled.

Exposure is mean(abs(inventory)) over all 240 end-of-batch observations before liquidation, including zeros. Peak absolute inventory is a secondary outcome; terminal flat inventory is not an exposure measure.

Each policy mean and each within-seed policy-minus-symmetric difference has a pointwise 95% Student-t interval: mean +/- t(0.975,31)*sample_sd/sqrt(32). Sample size and contrasts are fixed; no stopping or policy selection on results.

Fees are 0.05 tick per executed unit including liquidation. Terminal liquidation walks five refreshed levels of ten units at mid +/-3..7. Net already deducts fees and liquidation slippage; do not deduct liquidation cost again.
CSV includes levels and paired intervals for net, exposure, fees, liquidation cost and peak inventory. The full study JSON includes every seed's compact policy outcomes and evidence fingerprint.
limitations: Entirely synthetic exogenous flow with fully refreshed background depth; no calibration, endogenous market impact, funding, borrow cost or fee tiers. No live-market performance claim.
Intervals describe Monte Carlo uncertainty under the frozen simulator. They do not cover model error, and t coverage is approximate for non-normal seed outcomes.
Intervals are pointwise, without multiplicity adjustment across outcomes, policies or regimes. This is confirmation of specified contrasts, not a simultaneous ranking or risk-adjusted optimum.

Fresh seeds do not supply independent market data. The delayed policy measures five-batch refresh cadence, not the separate timestamped cancellation experiment. No illustrative replay is substituted for the 32-seed means.

cases.label: Event log / audit
cases.title: Can a saved stream reproduce the execution ledger?
cases.description: Compare direct execution with validated JSON replay on 48 synthetic buy/sell runs: TWAP and Sweep + retry, balanced/rising paths and capacity stress. Download the saved example and replay it without generating a market path.

event_log_evidence.assumptions: Synthetic finite-depth execution; direct in-memory baseline, same accepted commands; 0.05 tick per parent executed unit; zero funding/borrow costs. Replay requires no random seed. Fee sink is external.

method: Synthetic finite-depth execution; direct in-memory baseline, same accepted commands; 0.05 tick per parent executed unit; zero funding/borrow costs. Replay requires no random seed. Fee sink is external.

Strict versioned JSON with contiguous command sequence, typed integer prices/quantities, owner-checked cancellations and an explicit integer fee scale. Fresh-book replay verifies every trade, remaining FIFO order and account against a state digest.

Compare the original execution path with recording enabled/disabled, then compare parent fills, gross/net cash, inventory, fees and arrival shortfall with decoded replay. Four seeds 500..503, three scenarios, both sides and both policies; no runtime benchmark or statistical policy claim.
The downloadable seed-1729 TWAP log is read from disk and checked against a new direct run. Full-stream checksum detects accidental changes; the checkpoint detects replay differences.
limitations: Accepted book commands are sequential: this format does not preserve send/arrival timestamps, pending messages, reference marks, parent intent or random generator state. Shortfall also needs the explicitly retained arrival, terminal mark and parent quantity.

Checksums are not signatures or proof of authenticity. A producer can replace both stream and checkpoint. Replay tests internal reproducibility, not independent matching-engine correctness or real-market validity.
Synthetic flow, fully replenished finite depth, unlimited credit and shorting, self-trades allowed. Fees use integer hundredths here; the underlying book continues to report gross cash.

provenance: Entirely synthetic event stream. Matching uses the repository’s actual price/time-priority book; no fill-probability shortcut is used in these applied cases.
